figures.message: Given only noisy labels, one out-of-fold pass drops mostly mislabeled samples, and the refit model is more accurate than logistic regression on all noisy labels, though still short of the clean-label reference.
figures.layout:
Full width, about 6.9 in x 3.2 in, two rows: the filter on top, its two measured outcomes below. Plain sans-serif in regular weight, at least 7 pt at print size, no equations, no title above the figure. Three panel titles carry the three contributions in introduction order: '(a) Filter noisy labels' (a filter that needs only the noisy labels), '(b) What it removes' (what the filter drops), '(c) What it scores' (what the refit model gains and costs).

ROW 1, panel (a), full width, about 1.45 in tall: one flat pastel panel with rounded corners holding five equal tiles from left to right, joined by thick rounded arrows. Input tile, titled 'Noisy labels': schematic 2D scatter of two loose clusters, given class shown by marker only (filled dark circle vs open circle, achromatic so that no method colour stands for a class); three points deep inside the clusters carry the other cluster's marker, and one of them has a thin leader labelled 'Wrong label'. Under the scatter, two small outlined text pills, 'No clean set' and 'No noise rate', with no arrow into any stage. Stage 1, numbered circle 1, 'Predict out-of-fold': a strip of filter_folds equal fold blocks with the held-out block filled in the ours accent, a model card icon (a small card with an S-shaped curve) above the other blocks, and one curved arrow from the card into the held-out block. Stage 2, circle 2, 'Compare labels': three rows of marker pairs under the small column heads 'Given' and 'Predicted'; the one matching row ends in a check icon, the two differing rows end in a cross icon. Stage 3, circle 3, 'Drop mismatches': the input scatter again, with the three wrong-label points and one correctly labelled point just across the border between the clusters struck out by accent crosses; the correct one has a thin leader labelled 'Correct label, dropped'. Stage 4, circle 4, 'Refit once': only the kept points, one straight decision line in the ours accent between the clusters, and the same model card outlined in the accent. The parts that the method adds (held-out block, crosses, refit line, refit card) use the ours accent. The scatter positions are hand-placed and schematic.

ROW 2, about 1.6 in tall: panel (b) on the left (about 45% of the width) and panel (c) on the right (about 55%), both measured data, with the same six settings in the same order: Digits (Clean, 20%, 40%), small gap, Breast cancer (Clean, 20%, 40%). Dataset names are centred under their groups and each panel has the x label 'Training label noise'. The two x axes sit on one baseline.

Panel (b): y 'Training set removed (%)' from 0 to about 55. One stacked bar per setting, means over seeds. Bottom segment: mislabeled drops, solid ours accent. Top segment: correctly labeled drops, light tint of the accent with an accent edge, taken from the theme helpers. Clean settings have only the light segment, at the clean drop_fraction value. On each noisy setting a thick reference-gray horizontal tick, slightly wider than the bar and drawn over it, marks the mislabeled share of the whole training set (noisy_share keys), so a reader sees how close the solid segment comes to it. Legend above the axes: 'Dropped, mislabeled', 'Dropped, correctly labeled', 'All mislabeled'. No error bars.

Panel (c): y 'Test accuracy (%)' from 60 to 100 with an axis-break mark at the foot of the y axis (every seed value lies inside this range). Two bars per setting: logistic regression on all given labels (left, partner colour) and ours (right, ours accent); height is the seed mean, thin dark sd error bars with caps, five seed dots per bar (small, white fill, dark edge, fixed horizontal offsets by seed so that none hides the error bar). One reference-gray horizontal line per dataset group, spanning its three settings at the clean-label reference mean (the acc_logreg noise0 key of that dataset), drawn over the bars. Legend above the axes: 'Logistic regression', 'Ours', 'Clean-label reference'. Legends never overlap data, titles or each other.

figures.caption_draft: The out-of-fold filter (ours), the samples it removes and the test accuracy of the refit model. (a) A logistic regression fit on the other folds predicts each training sample (1), the prediction is compared with the given label (2), mismatches are dropped (3), and the model is refit once on the kept set (4). No stage reads a clean validation set, a noise rate or a confidence threshold. The points are schematic (filled and open mark the two given classes), and a correctly labeled sample can be dropped too. (b) Share of the training set removed, split into mislabeled and correctly labeled samples (means over 5 seeds); gray ticks mark the share of the whole training set that is mislabeled. Drops are few and all correctly labeled on clean labels. Under noise they are mostly mislabeled, and the solid segment comes close to the tick, least so on breast cancer at 40% noise. (c) Accuracy on clean test labels: bars are means over 5 seeds, error bars are sd, dots are seeds, and the y axis does not start at zero. Gray lines mark the clean-label reference (logistic regression trained on clean labels). Under noise ours has the higher mean in every setting, although five seeds do not establish the gain on breast cancer at 20% noise, and at 40% noise it stays below the gray line.

figures.message: Run by run on the same split, the filter beats logistic regression in all but one noisy run and stays near zero on clean labels.
figures.layout: Single column, about 3.25 in x 1.9 in. x: the six settings in the order of Fig. 1, Digits (Clean, 20%, 40%), small gap, Breast cancer (Clean, 20%, 40%), dataset names centred under their groups, x label 'Training label noise'. y: 'Gain of ours over' / 'logistic regression (points)' on two lines, from about -3 to 13 so that every seed value fits and zero is clearly visible. One bar per setting: the mean of the paired differences (ours minus logistic regression) in the ours accent. Thin dark error bars with caps: sd of the five paired differences. Five seed dots per bar (small, white fill, dark edge, fixed horizontal offsets by seed), drawn over the bar and the error bar so that the one noisy run below zero (breast cancer, 20%) is plainly visible. A reference-gray horizontal line at zero (equal to logistic regression), thicker than any grid line and drawn across the whole axis. The only plotted series is ours, so there is no legend; logistic regression is the zero line. No title and no text inside the axes.
figures.caption_draft: Paired gain in test accuracy of ours over logistic regression trained on all given labels. Each dot is one seed, with both methods on the same split and the same given labels; bars are means over 5 seeds, error bars are the sd of the paired differences, and the gray line marks no difference. Under noise the dots lie above zero in all but one run (breast cancer at 20% noise), including on breast cancer at 40% noise, where the accuracy of both methods varies widely between seeds. On clean labels the mean gain is close to zero.
